name: read_blueprint
description:
Read a Blueprint graph. Also handles Animation Blueprints (UAnimBlueprint).
Modes:
- "describe" (default): pseudo-code execution flow + node list. Use this FIRST to understand the graph. For Anim Blueprint graphs this renders an indented pose tree (sink first, pose inputs indented, bound assets in [brackets]); for a state-machine graph it lists entry->initial state, states (one-line content), conduits, aliases, and transitions (From -> To with crossfade/priority/auto-rule flags and a rule summary).
- "t3d": stripped T3D export. Use with "nodes" to get T3D for specific nodes you need to edit — add include_linked=true to also get their directly-connected neighbors (pins + links) in the same call. PREFER a nodes-filtered read over re-exporting the whole graph when you only need to check or wire a few nodes (e.g. right after insert_node). Without "nodes", exports the entire graph (may be large).
- "overview": full Blueprint structure (variables, functions, macros, components, interfaces, class settings). For Anim Blueprints this also reports the Target Skeleton and the anim-graph hierarchy (state machines, their states/transitions/conduits/aliases).

Graph addressing (the "graph" field): a flat graph name, OR a path "A/B/C" for nested graphs. For Anim Blueprints the default graph (omit "graph") is the AnimGraph. Nested anim graphs are addressed by path: "AnimGraph/Locomotion" (a state machine named by its node), "AnimGraph/Locomotion/Idle" (a state's bound graph), "AnimGraph/Locomotion/Idle->Walk" (a transition rule graph, addressed by ENDPOINTS — object names like "AnimationTransitionGraph_3" are opaque, so use From->To; append "#N" for duplicate pairs, "@blend" for a custom blend graph). A bare unique nested name also resolves; an ambiguous name returns an error listing the candidate paths.

Returns asset_revision: an opaque revision of the whole Blueprint package, including all graphs and Designer content. Pass the latest token as expected_revision on subsequent Blueprint or widget mutations. An intervening asset edit, rename, or replacement invalidates the token.

graph.description: Graph name or nested path "A/B/C". Defaults to "EventGraph" for ordinary Blueprints, or the "AnimGraph" for Animation Blueprints. Example anim paths: "AnimGraph/Locomotion" (state machine), "AnimGraph/Locomotion/Idle" (state), "AnimGraph/Locomotion/Idle->Walk" (transition rule, endpoint-addressed; "#N" for duplicates, "@blend" for a custom blend graph).

mode.description: "describe" for graph execution flow (default), "t3d" for T3D export, "overview" for full Blueprint structure (variables, functions, macros, components, interfaces, class settings).

nodes.description: Node names to export (t3d mode only). E.g. ["K2Node_Event_0", "K2Node_CallFunction_0"]. Omit for full graph.

include_linked.description: t3d mode with "nodes": also export every node directly linked to the named ones — one call shows a node plus its neighbors' real pins. Default false.

offset.description: Start index for T3D node pagination (t3d mode only). 0-based.

limit.description: Maximum number of T3D node blocks to return (t3d mode only). Default: all.

name: write_blueprint
description:
Inject T3D nodes into a Blueprint graph. Auto-compiles after injection.

## T3D Format
Each node is a Begin Object / End Object block. Pins are CustomProperties Pin lines.

## Template: Function Call (e.g. PrintString)
```
Begin Object Class=/Script/BlueprintGraph.K2Node_CallFunction Name="K2Node_CallFunction_NEW"
   FunctionReference=(MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary'",MemberName="PrintString")
   NodePosX=400
   NodePosY=0
   NodeGuid=GUID_MYNODE
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_EXEC_IN,PinName="execute",PinType.PinCategory="exec")
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_EXEC_OUT,PinName="then",Direction="EGPD_Output",PinType.PinCategory="exec")
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_SELF,PinName="self",PinType.PinCategory="object",PinType.PinSubCategoryObject="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary'",DefaultObject="/Script/Engine.Default__KismetSystemLibrary",bHidden=True)
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_INSTRING,PinName="InString",PinType.PinCategory="string",DefaultValue="Hello World")
End Object
```

## Template: Event (e.g. BeginPlay)
```
Begin Object Class=/Script/BlueprintGraph.K2Node_Event Name="K2Node_Event_NEW"
   EventReference=(MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.Actor'",MemberName="ReceiveBeginPlay")
   bOverrideFunction=True
   NodeGuid=GUID_BEGINPLAY
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_DELEGATE,PinName="OutputDelegate",Direction="EGPD_Output",PinType.PinCategory="delegate",PinType.PinSubCategoryMemberReference=(MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.Actor'",MemberName="ReceiveBeginPlay"))
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_THEN,PinName="then",Direction="EGPD_Output",PinType.PinCategory="exec")
End Object
```

## Template: Branch
```
Begin Object Class=/Script/BlueprintGraph.K2Node_IfThenElse Name="K2Node_IfThenElse_NEW"
   NodePosX=300
   NodeGuid=GUID_BRANCH
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_BR_EXEC,PinName="execute",PinType.PinCategory="exec")
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_BR_THEN,PinName="then",Direction="EGPD_Output",PinType.PinCategory="exec")
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_BR_ELSE,PinName="else",Direction="EGPD_Output",PinType.PinCategory="exec")
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_BR_COND,PinName="Condition",PinType.PinCategory="bool")
End Object
```
NOTE: Branch output exec pins are named "then" (true) and "else" (false) internally — NOT "True"/"False" (those are only display labels). Use "then"/"else" in edit_blueprint and T3D.

## Pin Categories (IMPORTANT)
- exec: execution flow pins
- bool: boolean
- int: integer
- real: float/double (use PinSubCategory="float" or "double")
- string: text
- name: FName
- object: UObject reference (needs PinSubCategoryObject)
- struct: struct reference (needs PinSubCategoryObject)
- delegate: delegate
NOTE: There is NO "float" category. Use PinCategory="real",PinSubCategory="float" for floats.

## Connection Rules
- Between NEW nodes in the same write_blueprint call: add LinkedTo=(TargetNodeName TargetPinId) using LINK_* placeholders on both sides — the plugin auto-creates reverse links
- To connect new nodes to EXISTING nodes: do NOT use LinkedTo — use edit_blueprint connect action after writing
- Use LINK_* placeholders for PinId, GUID_* for NodeGuid — they get resolved to real GUIDs

## Template: Pure Function Call (e.g. Multiply)
Pure functions have NO exec pins — only data pins. Use for math, getters, comparisons.
```
Begin Object Class=/Script/BlueprintGraph.K2Node_CallFunction Name="K2Node_Multiply_NEW"
   FunctionReference=(MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="Multiply_DoubleDouble")
   NodeGuid=GUID_MULTIPLY
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_SELF,PinName="self",PinType.PinCategory="object",PinType.PinSubCategoryObject=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',DefaultObject="/Script/Engine.Default__KismetMathLibrary",bHidden=True)
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_A,PinName="A",PinType.PinCategory="real",PinType.PinSubCategory="double",DefaultValue="0.0")
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_B,PinName="B",PinType.PinCategory="real",PinType.PinSubCategory="double",DefaultValue="0.0")
CustomProperties Pin (PinId=LINK_RET,PinName="ReturnValue",Direction="EGPD_Output",PinType.PinCategory="real",PinType.PinSubCategory="double")
End Object
```
IMPORTANT: Math functions use Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary' (with Class' prefix), NOT the /Script/CoreUObject.Class'...' format used for impure functions.

## Common Function References

Impure (have exec pins):
- PrintString: MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary'",MemberName="PrintString"
- GetActorLocation: MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.Actor'",MemberName="K2_GetActorLocation"
- SetActorLocation: MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.Actor'",MemberName="K2_SetActorLocation"
- DestroyActor: MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.Actor'",MemberName="K2_DestroyActor"
- Delay: MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary'",MemberName="Delay"
- IsValid: MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary'",MemberName="IsValid"
- SpawnActor: MemberParent="/Script/CoreUObject.Class'/Script/Engine.GameplayStatics'",MemberName="BeginDeferredActorSpawnFromClass"

String conversions (pure, KismetStringLibrary — use Class' prefix):
- Double/Float to String: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetStringLibrary',MemberName="Conv_DoubleToString" — input pin "InDouble" (PinCategory="real",PinSubCategory="double"), output "ReturnValue" (string). There is NO Conv_FloatToString in UE5.
- Int to String: MemberName="Conv_IntToString" — input "InInt" (int), output "ReturnValue" (string)
- Bool to String: MemberName="Conv_BoolToString" — input "InBool" (bool), output "ReturnValue" (string)
- Vector to String: MemberName="Conv_VectorToString" — input "InVec" (struct Vector), output "ReturnValue" (string)

Pure math (NO exec pins, use Class' prefix for MemberParent):
- Multiply: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="Multiply_DoubleDouble" — pins: A, B, ReturnValue (all real/double)
- Add: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="Add_DoubleDouble"
- Subtract: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="Subtract_DoubleDouble"
- Divide: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="Divide_DoubleDouble"
- Less Than: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="Less_DoubleDouble" — ReturnValue is bool
- Greater Than: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="Greater_DoubleDouble"
- Equal: MemberParent=Class'/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary',MemberName="EqualEqual_DoubleDouble"
- Int Add: MemberName="Add_IntInt" — pins: A, B, ReturnValue (all int)
- Int Multiply: MemberName="Multiply_IntInt"
- Bool AND: MemberName="BooleanAND" — A, B, ReturnValue (all bool)
- Bool OR: MemberName="BooleanOR"
- Bool NOT: MemberName="Not_PreBool" — A (bool), ReturnValue (bool)
- Clamp: MemberName="FClamp" — Value, Min, Max, ReturnValue (all real/double)
- Random Float: MemberName="RandomFloatInRange" — Min, Max, ReturnValue (all real/double)

Note: UE5 uses Double internally — "float" pins are PinCategory="real",PinSubCategory="double". There is no Multiply_FloatFloat — use Multiply_DoubleDouble.

## Animation graphs
Anim node T3D uses Class=/Script/AnimGraph.AnimGraphNode_* with the runtime struct serialized inline as Node=(...). Pose pins are PinType.PinCategory="struct" with PinSubCategoryObject pointing at FPoseLink (local space) or FComponentSpacePoseLink (component space). Prefer insert_node for anim nodes (it returns real pose pins). An anim graph also legally hosts PURE data K2 nodes (variable getters, pure functions, struct breaks, knots) — only IMPURE (exec) K2 nodes are rejected by the anim schema. A rejected node (an exec node injected into an anim graph, or any anim pose node injected into a K2 graph) is reported back as a schema-rejection warning with the node name — it is not silently kept.

expected_revision.description: Copy the latest asset_revision returned for this Blueprint package by a read or completed operation. The token covers the whole asset, including all graphs and the widget Designer, and is checked before mutation. On a revision conflict, reread the asset and replan; never retry the old operation automatically.

t3d.description: T3D text to inject. Use LINK_* for PinIds and GUID_* for NodeGuids.

auto_layout.description: When true, reformat the connected component(s) the new nodes joined after inserting them (tidies the graph). Overwrites existing node positions in those components, so leave false (default) unless you want the whole region re-laid-out.

name: compile_blueprint
description:
Compile a Blueprint and return structured errors/warnings. Use after modifications to verify correctness.
Also returns unreachable_node_warnings: exec node chains that are wired internally but have no exec path from any event or function entry (the compiler is silent about these — they look correct but never execute). Fix by wiring an exec output into the named pin, or delete the dead path.

expected_revision.description: Copy the latest asset_revision returned for this Blueprint package by a read or completed operation. The token covers the whole asset, including all graphs and the widget Designer, and is checked before mutation. On a revision conflict, reread the asset and replan; never retry the old operation automatically.

name: edit_blueprint
description:
Edit existing nodes in a Blueprint: connect/disconnect pins, set default values, delete nodes.
All operations are batched in one call, executed in order, then compiled. ALWAYS batch related operations in a single call.

Actions:
- "connect": Wire source_node.source_pin (output) → target_node.target_pin (input)
- "disconnect": Break link between source_node.source_pin → target_node.target_pin
- "set_pin_default": Set node.pin default value (e.g. change InString text, Duration, etc.). The value is validated against the pin type at edit time: a malformed value (bad struct literal, non-numeric number) fails with INVALID_DEFAULT and the pin keeps its previous value. Vector defaults use comma-separated X,Y,Z values, e.g. "1.0,0.0,0.0". Rotators use Pitch,Yaw,Roll, e.g. "0.0,90.0,0.0". LinearColor uses "(R=1.0,G=0.0,B=0.0,A=1.0)". Other structs use their UE text format; read the actual pin type before setting it
- "delete_node": Remove a node entirely

Example — insert Delay between BeginPlay and PrintString, change text:
{"operations": [
  {"action": "disconnect", "source_node": "K2Node_Event_0", "source_pin": "then", "target_node": "K2Node_CallFunction_0", "target_pin": "execute"},
  {"action": "connect", "source_node": "K2Node_Event_0", "source_pin": "then", "target_node": "K2Node_Delay_NEW", "target_pin": "execute"},
  {"action": "connect", "source_node": "K2Node_Delay_NEW", "source_pin": "then", "target_node": "K2Node_CallFunction_0", "target_pin": "execute"},
  {"action": "set_pin_default", "node": "K2Node_CallFunction_0", "pin": "InString", "value": "Delayed Hello"}
]}

Anim-oriented actions:
- "set_node_property": set a UPROPERTY on a NODE (not a pin), e.g. CacheName on a SaveCachedPose node, or a field inside the runtime struct via a dotted path "Node.GroupName" (the struct member is "Node" on most anim nodes, "BlendNode" on TwoWayBlend). Value is parsed with the property's own text format.
- "set_pin_visibility": expose/hide an anim node's "property as pin" (anim nodes only): {"action":"set_pin_visibility","node":"...","property":"Alpha","visible":true}. Exposes the pin so you can then wire or set it.
Pose connections use the same connect/disconnect actions — pose inputs are single-link and auto-break on reconnect.

expected_revision.description: Copy the latest asset_revision returned for this Blueprint package by a read or completed operation. The token covers the whole asset, including all graphs and the widget Designer, and is checked before mutation. On a revision conflict, reread the asset and replan; never retry the old operation automatically.

atomic.description: If true, revert the WHOLE batch when any operation fails (no half-wired state). The revert is verified against the pre-batch graph: rolled_back=true / outcome.recovery_status="restored" means the graph is exactly as before, so fix and resend. If recovery_status is "partially_restored" or "restore_failed" (retry_safe=false), part of the batch may remain: re-read the graph, do not resend. Refused with TRANSACTION_ACTIVE (nothing changed) while another editor transaction is open. Default false (best-effort: apply what succeeds).

operations.description: Array of edit operations to perform in order. BATCH all related edits in one call.

value.description: New value. For set_pin_default: pin default. For set_node_property: the property value in UE text format.

property.description: Property name for set_node_property / set_pin_visibility. set_node_property accepts a dotted path into the runtime struct, e.g. "Node.GroupName".

visible.description: For set_pin_visibility: true to expose the property as a pin, false to hide it.

name: insert_node

expected_revision.description: Copy the latest asset_revision returned for this Blueprint package by a read or completed operation. The token covers the whole asset, including all graphs and the widget Designer, and is checked before mutation. On a revision conflict, reread the asset and replan; never retry the old operation automatically.

graph.description: Graph name or path. Defaults to "EventGraph" (or the AnimGraph for an Animation Blueprint). Nested anim graphs are addressable by path, e.g. "AnimGraph/Locomotion/Idle".

node.description: The node's menu name as it appears in the Blueprint right-click menu, e.g. "ForEachLoop", "Branch", "Print String", "Cast to BP_Enemy", "Switch on Int".

class.description: Optional class filter to disambiguate a function node (e.g. "KismetMathLibrary", "Actor").

node_class.description: Optional node-CLASS filter, for when one menu name maps to more than one node type (distinct from "class", which filters a function's owning class). Example: an input axis exposes BOTH a value getter (K2Node_GetInputAxisValue) and an event (K2Node_InputAxisEvent) under the same name — pass "K2Node_InputAxisEvent" to get the event. The "K2Node_" prefix is optional. The response's node_class field reports which type you actually got, so if it is not the one you wanted, retry with this filter.

connect_from.description: Optional: wire an exec output of an EXISTING node into this node's exec input. Connecting an already-linked exec output breaks its old link — set splice=true to re-route that link through the new node instead (insert into the chain).

pin.description: Source output pin name. Defaults to "then".

splice.description: Insert into the existing chain: the pin's previous target is re-wired to the new node's 'then' (or first exec output). Default false.

connect_to.description: Optional: wire this NEW node's first compatible OUTPUT pin into an EXISTING node's input. The mirror of connect_from, for the common "this node feeds a downstream node" case. Works for exec, pose, and data pins — the schema picks the compatible pair. PREFER passing connect_to (or connect_from) over a separate edit_blueprint connect: a node wired at insert time lands right next to the node it feeds, instead of stranded across the canvas. If the new node ends up unwired (target/pin not found or incompatible) it is still inserted and the result message says so — then wire it with edit_blueprint.

node.description: Existing target node name (e.g. "K2Node_CallFunction_2") whose input pin the new node should feed.

pin.description: Target input pin name. Optional — omit to auto-pick the first schema-compatible input on the target.

auto_layout.description: When true, reformat the connected component the new node joined after inserting it (tidies that region). Overwrites existing node positions in the component, so leave false (default) unless a re-layout is wanted.

name: search_assets

class_filter.description: Filter by asset class: Blueprint, WidgetBlueprint, AnimBlueprint, UserDefinedStruct, UserDefinedEnum, DataTable, Material, Texture2D, StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, SoundWave, World, AnimSequence, AnimMontage, AnimComposite, BlendSpace, BlendSpace1D, AimOffsetBlendSpace, AimOffsetBlendSpace1D, Skeleton

path.description: Content path to search in, e.g. /Game/Characters. Recursive by default.

parent_class.description: For Blueprints: filter by parent class (e.g. Character, Actor, Pawn, ActorComponent)

name: read_source

mode.description: "find" to search for files, "outline" to extract declarations (default), "raw" for full content with line numbers.

file.description: Path to source file (outline/raw modes). Absolute, project-relative (e.g. "ParkourGame/Public/Player/PGPawn.h"), or engine-relative (e.g. "Runtime/Engine/Classes/GameFramework/Actor.h").

pattern.description: Basename glob using literals, * and ?. No **, paths, character classes or braces; 1–128 characters. Broad extension globs such as *.h use the same work budgets in every scope.

scope.description: Explicit scope confines discovery and reads to project Source, engine Source, or engine/project Plugins and discovered plugins. Omitted scope admits their union; relative reads still resolve against project.

query.description: Filter outline results by keyword (case-insensitive). E.g. "Jump" shows only jump-related declarations.

offset.description: Start line (0-based) for raw mode pagination. Default: 0.

limit.description: Max raw lines or outline declarations (default 200, max 500). Find pages contain at most 20 files and may stop earlier at a work/output budget.

cursor.description: Opaque single-use find continuation; repeat identical pattern, scope and limit. Expires after 60 seconds idle.

request_id.description: Optional REST source-job identifier (at most 128 characters), used by /api/v1/read_source/cancel.

name: read_logs
description:
Read/grep the current editor session's Unreal log (Saved/Logs/<Project>.log) — the real engine output: compile messages, Blueprint runtime errors, asset/load warnings, PIE output, and plugin logs. Use this to see what an action actually produced beyond the compile result (why something failed at runtime, asset-load warnings, or to find a specific Print String / log line).

All fields optional:
- level: minimum severity — "error", "warning" (default), "display", "all". Use "all" with a pattern to find non-warning output (e.g. Print String).
- pattern: a regular expression matched against each line (e.g. "BP_Player|failed to load").
- category: substring of the log line/category (e.g. "LogBlueprint", "LogCompile", "PIE", "LogLinker").
- lines: max lines to return (default 100, max 500).
- tail: return the LAST matching lines (default true) or the first.

Returns the matching lines (most recent last), total matched, a truncated flag, and the log path. Scans the last few MB of the log.

Examples:
- {} — recent warnings + errors
- {"level": "error"} — recent errors only
- {"pattern": "BP_Player", "level": "all"} — everything mentioning BP_Player
- {"category": "LogBlueprintUserMessages", "level": "all"} — Print String / user log output

pattern.description: Regular expression matched against each log line.

category.description: Substring filter, e.g. LogBlueprint, LogCompile, PIE, LogLinker.

tail.description: Return the last matching lines (default true) or the first.

name: enter_plan_mode
description: Enter Plan first, the read-only planning mode for asset changes. Use when the user explicitly asks to plan first, or when ambiguity would risk substantial rework before the user reviews the approach. After this tool succeeds, you may only use read-only exploration tools until you call exit_plan_mode.

name: exit_plan_mode
description: Exit planning mode with a final plan for user approval. Call this only after entering plan mode, completing read-only exploration, and writing a concise asset-focused implementation plan. Do not ask for plan approval in plain text; this tool is the approval boundary.

title.description: Short human-readable plan title (becomes the card heading and file slug).

description.description: One- or two-sentence summary of the intended gameplay or editor behavior.

body.description: A concise asset-focused plan in markdown: intended behavior; concrete asset paths and graphs to create or modify; important design choices and existing logic to reuse, preserve, or replace; and verification steps. Distinguish existing assets from proposed new ones. Include node-level detail only when it explains a decision.

plan.description: Deprecated — use `body`. Accepted for backwards compatibility.

name: ask_user
description: Ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions and wait for their answer. Use ONLY when a requirement is genuinely ambiguous and choosing wrong would cause real rework — e.g. multiple valid Blueprint approaches, an unclear target asset/graph, or a destructive/irreversible change. First explore with read-only tools; ask only what you cannot determine yourself. Do NOT use this to request permission to do what the user already asked, and do NOT use it as a reflex to avoid simple decisions. The user can always pick 'Other' and type a custom answer. If no user is available the tool returns immediately and you should proceed on your best judgment.

question.description: The question text, phrased clearly and specifically.

header.description: A short label for this question (max ~12 chars), e.g. "Parent class".

label.description: Concise choice text shown to the user.

description.description: Optional one-line explanation of this choice / its trade-off.

multiSelect.description: Set true if the user may pick more than one option. Defaults to false.

name: update_todos
description: Maintain a visible checklist for GENUINELY multi-step Blueprint work (5+ distinct tool-using steps, e.g. several variables + functions + multiple graphs wired). Call it when you start such a task to lay out the steps, and again after each step to update status — mark a step in_progress BEFORE working on it and completed IMMEDIATELY after, keeping exactly one in_progress at a time. Do NOT call it for short tasks (a few nodes, a single graph edit) — it only adds overhead. The final step of any tracked task should be a verification step (e.g. read_blueprint + compile_blueprint).

todos.description: The full current todo list (send the entire list every time, not a delta).

content.description: Imperative form of the step, e.g. "Wire BeginPlay to PrintString".

activeForm.description: Present-continuous form shown while active, e.g. "Wiring BeginPlay to PrintString".

name: discover_tools
description:
Load an extended tool so it becomes available for use. Extended tools are not loaded by default to keep the context efficient.

Available extended tools:
- manage_blueprint: Structural Blueprint operations — add/remove variables, functions, macros, custom events, event dispatchers, interfaces, change parent class
- manage_components: Actor components — add/remove/reparent components, and set default properties, collision, materials, and post-process materials (blendables) on components from this Blueprint, a parent Blueprint, or a native C++ parent. Prefer this over runtime nodes (e.g. AddOrUpdateBlendable at BeginPlay) when the user wants a component's defaults changed.
- manage_state_machine: Animation Blueprint state machines — create a state machine in the AnimGraph, add states/conduits/aliases/transitions, set transition properties, set the entry state, rename and delete states/transitions.
- manage_animation: Edit animation ASSETS (not Blueprints) — montages (slot tracks, segments, sections, sync group), anim sequences + montages (notifies), blend spaces (axes, samples). Also reads their structure via the 'get' action. Create the assets first with create_asset (AnimMontage/AnimSequence/BlendSpace/…).

Categories (load several related tools at once):
- blueprint_tools: manage_blueprint + manage_components + manage_state_machine + layout_graph
- project_tools: get_references + create_asset + manage_asset + manage_animation
- discovery_tools: search_nodes + inspect_class
- material_tools: read_material + create_material_expression + edit_material + compile_material + create_material_instance + set_material_instance_parameter + manage_material
- widget_tools: read_widget + edit_widget (UMG Widget Blueprint Designer hierarchy — the widget tree and slot layout)

Call this BEFORE using any of these tools. The tool becomes available on your next response.

Workflow:
1. read_blueprint(mode="overview") to see current Blueprint structure
2. discover_tools("manage_blueprint") to load structural operations
3. manage_blueprint(...) to make structural changes
4. write_blueprint(graph="NewFunction") to populate new function graphs

tool_name.description: Name of the extended tool to load, or a category that loads several at once (blueprint_tools, project_tools, discovery_tools, material_tools, widget_tools)
